Three-year committed facility provides MetaOptics with flexible growth capital, drawn down at the Company's sole discretion

SINGAPORE, Nov. 22, 2026 /PRNewswire/ -- MetaOptics Ltd (Catalist: 9MT) (OTCQX: MOTLY) ("MetaOptics" or the "Company", and together with its subsidiaries, the "Group"), a Singapore-headquartered semiconductor optics company pioneering glass-based metalens solutions enhanced by AI-driven image processing, announced that it had on 20 November 2026, entered into a share subscription facility agreement with GEM Opportunities Fund ISA Ltd. ("GEM"), the Bermuda-based investment vehicle managed by Global Emerging Markets (GEM), New York, for an aggregate commitment of up to S$32 million (the "Share Subscription Facility"). The Share Subscription Facility is subject to, inter alia, the approval of the Company's shareholders ("Shareholders") at an extraordinary general meeting ("EGM") to be convened. A circular containing further details of the Share Subscription Facility, together with the notice of EGM, will be despatched to Shareholders in due course.

The Company intends to apply the net proceeds from drawdowns under the Share Subscription Facility, entirely for the Group's working capital purposes, including general corporate expenses, funding the day-to-day operations of the Group and supporting the growth of its existing business. As part of the Group's plans to grow its existing business, the Group intends to establish a new 12-inch glass semiconductor fabrication line in the United States to produce metalenses for co-packaged optics ("CPO") and colour imaging applications. The Share Subscription Facility provides MetaOptics with flexible access to growth capital while allowing the Company to control the timing of any drawdowns, in line with its capital needs and prevailing market conditions.

Mr Thng Chong Kim, Executive Chairman of MetaOptics, said: "This Share Subscription Facility gives us a reliable, flexible source of capital for our day-to-day operations and to support the growth of our existing business by establishing a new 12-inch glass semiconductor fabrication line in the United States, on terms that put MetaOptics in control of the timing and size of each drawdown. We are pleased to have the backing of GEM, an experienced global investor, as we execute on our plans and build long-term value for our Shareholders."

This press release should be read in conjunction with the announcement released by the Company on SGXNet on 23 November 2026 in relation to the Share Subscription Facility.

About MetaOptics Ltd
MetaOptics Ltd (Catalist: 9MT) is a leading-edge semiconductor optics company pioneering glass-based metalens solutions enhanced by AI-driven image processing. Using advanced optical design and a scalable 12-inch DUV lithography process, it powers next-generation applications in CPO, mobile, AR/VR, automotive and other emerging markets. Headquartered in Singapore, MetaOptics aims to deliver high-performance optics with the reliability and scalability demanded by today's most innovative technology brands. Find out more at www.metaoptics.sg.

About GEM
GEM (Global Emerging Markets) is a US$3.4 billion alternative investment group with operations in Paris, New York, Los Angeles and the Bahamas. GEM manages a diverse set of investment vehicles focused on emerging and developed markets and has completed over 600 transactions in 75 countries. Each investment vehicle has a different degree of operational control, risk-adjusted return and liquidity profile. Its family of funds and investment vehicles provides GEM and its partners with exposure to Small-Mid Cap Management Buyouts, Private Investments in Public Equities and select venture investments.  For more information, please visit www.gemny.com.

HONG KONG and SHANGHAI and FLORHAM PARK, N.J., Nov. 22, 2026 (GLOBE NEWSWIRE) -- HUTCHMED (China) Limited (“HUTCHMED”) (Nasdaq/AIM:​HCM; HKEX:​13) today announces that it has initiated RANOVA, a registrational Phase III clinical trial of ranosidenib (HMPL-306) in patients with postoperative residual or recurrent Grade 2 gliomas harboring isocitrate dehydrogenase (“IDH”) 1 or 2 mutations in China. Ranosidenib is a novel, highly potent and selective dual inhibitor of IDH1 and IDH2 mutant enzymes. The first patient received the first dose on November 20, 2026.

Gliomas are the most common primary brain tumors, representing around 80% of all primary malignant and central nervous system tumors.1 Worldwide, it is estimated that approximately 260,000 new cases of glioma are diagnosed annually, including nearly 70,000 in China. 2,3 IDH1 or IDH2 mutations are recognized as key oncogenic drivers in the pathogenesis and progression of glioma, found in approximately 70% to 80% of Grade 2 or 3 gliomas, including astrocytoma and oligodendroglioma.4

The trial is a randomized, double-blind, placebo-controlled, multicenter Phase III study evaluating the efficacy and safety of oral ranosidenib versus placebo in participants with postoperative residual or recurrent Grade 2 astrocytoma or oligodendroglioma carrying IDH1 or IDH2 mutations who have previously received only surgical treatment. Following Blinded Independent Review Committee (“BIRC”)-confirmed disease progression, eligible participants in the placebo group may cross over to receive ranosidenib.

The primary outcome measure is progression-free survival (“PFS”) assessed by BIRC according to Response Assessment in Neuro-Oncology (RANO) 2.0 criteria. Secondary outcome measures include investigator-assessed PFS, time to next intervention (TTNI), tumor growth rate (TGR), objective response rate (ORR), overall survival (OS), safety, and quality of life. Additional details may be found at clinicaltrials.gov, using identifier NCT07912398.

This registrational trial plans to enroll approximately 210 patients in China. The leading principal investigators are Professor Jinsong Wu of Huashan Hospital, Fudan University and Professor Xiaohui Ren of Capital Medical University Beijing Tiantan Hospital.

About Ranosidenib

Ranosidenib is a novel dual-inhibitor of IDH1 and IDH2 mutant enzymes. Mutations of IDH1 and IDH2 have been implicated as drivers of certain hematological malignancies, gliomas and solid tumors. Cytoplasmic mutant IDH1 and mitochondrial mutant IDH2 have been known to switch to the other form when targeted by an inhibitor of IDH1 mutant alone or IDH2 mutant alone. Targeting both IDH1 and IDH2 mutations may provide therapeutic benefits in cancer patients by overcoming this acquired resistance.

HUTCHMED currently retains all rights to ranosidenib worldwide.

About HUTCHMED

HUTCHMED (Nasdaq/AIM:HCM; HKEX:13) is an innovative, commercial-stage, biopharmaceutical company. It is committed to the discovery and global development and commercialization of targeted therapies and immunotherapies for the treatment of cancer and immunological diseases. Since inception it has focused on bringing drug candidates from in-house discovery to patients around the world, with its first five medicines marketed in China, the first of which is also approved around the world including in the US, Europe and Japan. PARIS--(BUSINESS WIRE)--TotalEnergies (Paris:TTE) (LSE:TTE) (NYSE:TTE) has signed a new agreement with Continental Resources, under which TotalEnergies acquires interests in natural gas upstream assets. The transaction is expected to add approximately 150 MMscf/d1 (equivalent to around 26 kboe/d) to TotalEnergies’ net gas production in the United States by 2032.

“We are pleased to further expand our cooperation with Continental Resources, a leading U.S. operator in the region. This transaction will strengthen our natural gas production in the United States and consolidate TotalEnergies’ integrated position from Upstream gas production to LNG exports,” said Nicolas Terraz, President Exploration & Production at TotalEnergies.

TotalEnergies’ natural gas production in the U.S.

This transaction with Continental Resources builds on previous acquisitions of non-operated interests completed in 2025 in the Anadarko Basin with Continental Resources and in 2024 in the Eagle Ford play with EOG Resources and Lewis Energy. These assets will offer low-cost, low-emission, long-plateau production and are well connected to existing midstream infrastructure. Together with TotalEnergies’ operated Barnett asset, they are expected to bring the Company’s overall net natural gas production in the U.S. to approximately 850 MMscf/d2 (equivalent to more than 140 kboe/d) from 2032 onwards.

TotalEnergies’ LNG Activities in the U.S.

TotalEnergies is the number one exporter of U.S. LNG with 19 million tons exported in 2025, representing 18% of the whole U.S. production, out of which 14 million tons for Europe. The Company is integrated throughout the LNG value chain, with upstream gas production assets in Texas, Oklahoma and offshore U.S. TotalEnergies has invested in a number of major LNG projects in the U.S. including Cameron LNG and Rio Grande LNG. TotalEnergies also offtakes LNG from major U.S. terminals, such as Sabine Pass LNG, Freeport LNG, and Corpus Christi LNG.

VANCOUVER, BC, Nov. 22, 2026 /PRNewswire/ -- Luca Mining Corp. ("Luca" or the "Company") (TSXV: LUCA) (OTCQX: LUCMF) (Frankfurt: Z68) wishes to clarify recent reports published by various Mexican media outlets stating that the Company's Campo Morado Mine, located in Arcelia, Guerrero State, Mexico, is controlled by a criminal organization.

These reports are categorically false. The Campo Morado Mine is owned and operated by Luca through its wholly owned subsidiary, Minas de Campo Morado, S.A. de C.V., and Luca has sole operational and financial control of the mine. Neither Luca nor any of its directors, officers or employees has any affiliation with the individuals mentioned in those reports.

Luca is not aware of any active or, to its knowledge, pending investigation by any authority in connection with these matters at its Campo Morado Mine. The Company believes the source of the reports may have confused Luca's business and affairs with other mining operations near the town of Campo Morado, which is unconnected with the Campo Morado mine, and with which Luca has no operational history.

Minas de Campo Morado, S.A. de C.V. operates under valid federal mining concessions and environmental permits, is subject to oversight by Mexican authorities, including the Army Ministry for the use of explosives in the mine, sells its concentrates to an established international buyer, and continues to operate in the normal course. Luca has formally requested that the outlets reporting on the Campo Morado mine correct their reports. Luca reiterates its commitment to transparency and will cooperate with the authorities if requested.

Luca Mining Corp. (TSX-V: LUCA, OTCQX: LUCMF, Frankfurt: Z68) is a Canadian mining company with two wholly owned mines located in the prolific Sierra Madre mineralized belt in Mexico. The Company's Campo Morado Mine hosts VMS-style, polymetallic mineralization within a large land package comprising 121 square kilometres. It is an underground operation, producing zinc, copper, gold, silver and lead. The mine is located in Guerrero State.

The Tahuehueto Mine is a large property of over 100 square kilometres in Durango State. The project hosts epithermal gold and silver vein-style mineralization. LOS ANGELES, Nov. 22, 2026 /PRNewswire/ -- FF EAI Robotics Ecosystem Inc. (NASDAQ: FFR) ("FFR" or the "Company"), a U.S.-based Embodied AI ("EAI") robotics company, today shared a weekly business update from YT Jia, Founder and Global CEO of FF and FFR.

"Welcome to my 82nd weekly report. Let me start with three major breakthroughs for FFR's education ecosystem in U.S. K–12 and career education. First, FFR is now an approved robotics supplier to a public school district that is considered top-tier both nationally and within California. We've cleared the district's review and joined its procurement platform. That means more than 1,000 schools in the district can now purchase FFR robots and our education productivity solutions directly. This week, the district's career education center led the way by purchasing several robots, including FX Navi and Aegis EDU. We hope the project will serve as a model for a broader rollout across the district.

Second, we signed a Strategic Education Partnership Framework Agreement with another public school district, one of California's leading districts. The district has also purchased robot devices including Master Mini and Aegis EDU. Third, we signed a Strategic Education Partnership Framework Agreement with an additional major public school district in Los Angeles.

The second and third partnerships both cover K–12 through adult education. We'll work with the two districts to develop curricula together, set up innovation labs, create career and technical education pathways, train teachers, and give students hands-on experience. Together, we'll explore how Physical AI education can connect what students learn in the classroom with further study, real-world practice, and career development. These two collaborations both renew automatically at the end of their terms. With these frameworks in place, we can move future projects forward quickly through a streamlined process.

Outside of California, we are also moving forward with strategic partnerships and sales in robotics education across multiple school districts in four other states: New York, Pennsylvania, Florida, and Texas. FFR pioneered K–12 robotics education in the U.S., and we're now No. 1 in the industry. The progress we've made on strategic partnerships and robot purchases across these three leading districts matters to FFR and to the whole industry. Let me share four reasons why:

First, it's a big step forward for our education ecosystem. By working with major school districts as strategic partners at the school district level, we can work directly with the U.S. public education system to build Physical AI education pathways that connect K–12 learning, technical skills training, and future careers.

Second, these projects give us a model for replicating at scale nationwide. The U.S. has more than 13,000 regular public-school districts. Across the country, about 130,000 public and private K–12 schools serve roughly 53 million students. That's a large market, with opportunities across robot devices, curricula, teacher training, and ongoing services. We'll learn from our first projects with leading districts, turn what works into a repeatable model, and gradually roll it out to across the country.

Third, it helps us move faster on our Four-Core Full-Stack AI business in education and speeds up the evolutionary flywheel. Four operational filter presses achieve a key filtration requirement toward commercial production

VANCOUVER, British Columbia, Nov. 23, 2026 (GLOBE NEWSWIRE) -- Eldorado Gold Corporation (TSX: ELD, NYSE: EGO) (“Eldorado” or the “Company”) is pleased to announce that four tailings filter presses are now operational at its Skouries mine in northern Greece, marking another important milestone in the commissioning and ramp-up of the operation.

“With four filter presses now operational, we have achieved another important milestone in the ramp-up of Skouries,” said Christian Milau, President and Chief Executive Officer. “With this additional filtration capacity now online, we are well positioned to advance throughput and build momentum across the operation. We remain focused on progressing the ramp-up toward commercial production, which we expect late this quarter.”

Four operating filter presses are required to support commercial production on sulphide ore, with five required to achieve nameplate throughput. The Skouries tailings filtration facility comprises six Metso filter presses, including five operating units and one installed spare. The sixth unit provides operational flexibility and enables maintenance activities with no loss of throughput. The remaining two filter presses are expected to be operational in early December.

Technical Report

Eldorado expects to file an updated Technical Report for Skouries in the first quarter of 2027, incorporating an updated resource model and metal price assumptions, together with updated production, operating cost and capital estimates reflecting the transition of Skouries from development into operations.

Eldorado is a gold, copper and base metals producer with mining, development and exploration operations in Canada, Türkiye, and Greece. The Company has a highly skilled and dedicated workforce, safe and responsible operations, a portfolio of high-quality assets, and long-term partnerships with local communities. LONDON--(BUSINESS WIRE)--Smartphone shipments in Africa fell 40% year-on-year (YoY) to 13.7 million units, down from 22.8 million a year earlier, according to Omdia’s latest research. This marked the steepest YoY decline in three years following three consecutive years of third-quarter growth. Rising component costs and currency pressures are changing how vendors price their devices and how consumers buy them across Africa's largest markets.

Africa smartphone market shipment, 2Q23 to 3Q26

Rising prices weigh on smartphone shipments and market value

Shipments of smartphones priced below $100 fell nearly 70% YoY in 3Q26, while feature phone shipments grew 27%. Entry-level smartphones are becoming less profitable, prompting vendors to reconsider which models they offer and how they price them. Consumers who pay in cash, particularly those without access to operator subsidies or financing, are delaying upgrades or turning to refurbished smartphones and feature phones. Higher-priced smartphones are increasingly out of reach for these buyers.

“The figures show how affordability is shaping buying decisions in Africa. Some buyers are waiting longer to upgrade or choosing a refurbished smartphone to stay within budget,” notes Manish Pravinkumar, Principal Analyst at Omdia. “In many other regions, higher average selling prices (ASPs) helped sustain market value as shipments fell. In Africa, the ASP reached $222 in 3Q26, its highest third-quarter level in a decade. Even so, market value fell 15%. The increase in average price reflects a widening affordability gap and offers little evidence that buyers are moving to more expensive models.”

Nigeria and Egypt record the steepest shipment declines among Africa’s key markets

The size of the decline varied across Africa's key markets, reflecting differences in economic conditions, access to consumer financing, and exposure to currency and policy changes. Nigeria recorded the steepest decline among these markets, with smartphone shipments down 47% YoY. Fuel price pressures following subsidy removal, limited access to US dollars for import payments and higher handset costs further reduced household purchasing power.

In Egypt, smartphone shipments fell 41%. A weaker Egyptian pound and persistent inflation raised the cost of importing phones and manufacturing them locally, prompting consumers to delay upgrades.

In Kenya, smartphone shipments fell 35%. Shipments in the country’s core price segment, smartphones priced below $150, fell 44% as higher device prices put these devices beyond the reach of more buyers. Credit purchases and instalment plans are playing a growing role in helping consumers manage upfront costs.

South Africa recorded a smaller decline of 20%. Established operator distribution networks, contract upgrades, and a wider range of retail channels helped support shipments. High smartphone penetration, pressure on household budgets and longer replacement cycles continued to weigh on demand.

Samsung gains market share as TRANSSION retains the lead

TRANSSION accounted for 48% of smartphone shipments in Africa in 3Q26. Its shipments fell 43%, reflecting its exposure to the shrinking market for smartphones priced below $100.

Samsung recorded the smallest shipment decline among the five leading vendors, down 8%, and its market share rose to 23%. Its operator relationships and broad Galaxy A-series portfolio supported shipments. The Galaxy A07 4G and A17 4G together accounted for 56% of Samsung’s total smartphone shipments in Africa during the quarter.

Xiaomi’s shipments fell 49% as price increases across its portfolio weakened demand from channel partners and reduced its share of consumer spending.

HONOR’s shipments fell 14% YoY in 3Q26 after recording near triple-digit growth in the previous two years. Its performance in South Africa and expansion into other African markets supported that earlier growth. The decline shows how higher handset prices can slow even fast-growing vendors.

OPPO’s shipments fell 69% as it reorganized its operations as part of its integration with realme.

Tax reforms and device financing offer potential routes to recovery

Omdia expects smartphone shipments in Africa to end 2026 down 23% YoY and forecasts a further 25% decline in 2027.

“The forecast shows how heavily Africa's smartphone market depends on affordable devices and continued growth in shipments,” said Pravinkumar. “With cost pressures expected to persist into 2027, vendors face a difficult pricing challenge. They need to keep entry-level devices profitable, but passing higher component costs on to buyers risks putting smartphones beyond the reach of more households.”

Tax policy and access to financing will also shape the prospects for a recovery. Morocco reduced its smartphone import duty from 17.5% to 2.5%, illustrating how tax reform can ease cost pressures. Vodacom has introduced prepaid handset financing across all its African markets. In Nigeria, vivo is working with Credit Direct on device financing. M-KOPA continues to expand its smartphone financing model.

Pravinkumar added, “Governments, manufacturers and mobile operators all have a role in improving affordability. Closer cooperation will be essential to expand local manufacturing, make distribution more cost-effective, and give more customers access to financing. The next phase of growth depends on making connected devices affordable for a wider range of buyers.”

Vancouver, BC – TheNewswire - November 23, 2026 – Uranium One Mining Corp. ("Uranium One" or the "Company") (UUU: CSE | UUUFF: OTCID | SL5: Frankfurt) is pleased to announce the appointment of Jeremy S. Brett, M.Sc., P.Geo., as a technical advisor. Mr. Brett has been involved with the Company’s recently acquired Pasfield Lake Uranium Project in Saskatchewan’s Athabasca Basin for more than two decades. He will draw on that experience to advise the Company on reviewing historical exploration records and planning future exploration of the project.

Mr. Brett’s technical and exploration background Includes:

  • More than 30 years of international mineral exploration experience as a Senior Geophysical Consultant, in all geophysical methods and most commodities on five continents 

  • Consulting experience with more than 100 leading junior and major exploration and mining companies, as well as provincial and national governments, in Canada and internationally 

  • M.Sc. in Geology (Geophysics) and B.Sc. in Physics (Geophysics) from the University of Toronto 

  • Professional Geoscientist (P.Geo.) registered with Professional Geoscientists Ontario 

  • Extensive experience consulting to and directing geophysical and geological exploration programs 

  • Uranium experience in Athabasca-type and other uranium settings in Canada and internationally 

  • Served on the board of directors of the Prospectors and Developers Association of Canada (PDAC) 

  • Expertise in integrating geophysical, geological and physical-properties data with ore deposit models and structural geology to identify and test exploration targets 

David Greenway, Chief Executive Officer of Uranium One, commented: “Jeremy’s appointment brings valuable technical expertise and more than two decades of familiarity with Pasfield Lake to Uranium One. His experience integrating geophysical and geological data will help guide our evaluation of the project’s extensive historical exploration database and refine priorities for future exploration. As we advance our Athabasca Basin portfolio, we are focused on building the technical foundation needed to identify and systematically test compelling uranium targets.”

Biography

Mr. Brett is a Senior Geophysical Consultant who has designed, supervised, quality-assured and interpreted exploration programs for uranium, copper and a broad range of other commodities in North, Central and South America, Africa, Asia, Europe and the Middle East. He has advised more than 100 junior and major exploration and mining companies, as well as provincial and national governments. He has also served as the geophysics champion for the PDAC Exploration Assessment Digital Data Formats working group. His experience includes exploration program design, project management, data integration, target prioritization and target testing. He is familiar with the reporting requirements under National Instrument 43-101.

Mr. Brett specializes in integrating geophysical, geological and physical-properties data with ore deposit models and structural geology to identify and test exploration targets. He is a Professional Geoscientist (P.Geo.) registered with Professional Geoscientists Ontario. He is a Fellow of the Society of Economic Geologists (SEG) and a member of the Canadian Exploration Geophysical Society (KEGS), Professional Engineers & Geoscientists Newfoundland & Labrador (PEGNL), and the Prospectors and Developers Association of Canada (PDAC).

NORWICH, England--(BUSINESS WIRE)--Cadeler has published its Q3 2026 Earnings Release, reflecting continued strong performance, with revenue for the third quarter up by 65% compared to the same period in 2025. The quarter saw further expansion of the fleet and of the company’s capabilities: In July, Cadeler took delivery of its second A-class vessel, Wind Ace, and in August it acquired Menck, strengthening its full-scope foundation installation offering.

Revenue for the first nine months of 2026 reached EUR 663 million, up 94% from EUR 342 million for the same period last year, while EBITDA was EUR 321 million, up 52% from EBITDA of EUR 211 million in 2025 (in each case, when adjusting for one-off termination fees of EUR 111 million in the comparative period).

Profit for the first nine months of 2026 was EUR 143 million, up 18% from EUR 121 million in the comparative period, when adjusting for the termination fees identified above.

Utilisation of Cadeler’s 11 vessels was 69.8%, compared with 75.8% across eight operating vessels over the same period last year, while contracted days increased by 44%, reflecting increased activity across the enlarged fleet.

Cadeler maintains its full-year 2026 guidance, with full-year revenue expected to be within the range of EUR 910 million to 1,000 million, which includes an anticipated hammer sale scheduled to complete in December 2026. Full-year EBITDA is expected to be within the range of EUR 435 million to 525 million, when excluding costs related to the acquisition and integration of Menck.

Mikkel Gleerup, CEO of Cadeler, comments:

“These results demonstrate that our strategy is translating into strong execution and continued growth. During the period, we have delivered solid operational and financial performance, welcomed Wind Ace to our fleet and, through the acquisition of Menck, significantly strengthened the capabilities we can offer within full-scope foundation transport and installation. Together, these developments give us greater flexibility to respond to changing project requirements and support our customers with the reliability, resilience and certainty of delivery they increasingly require. With a strong backlog and continued demand for our vessels and services, we remain focused on disciplined execution across our projects while building the capabilities required for the next phase of offshore wind development.”

Acquisition of Menck

Cadeler completed the acquisition of Menck in August 2026 for an enterprise value of EUR 501 million. The acquisition combines Menck’s specialist equipment and engineering expertise with Cadeler’s installation fleet and experience, enabling a more integrated foundation installation offering for the group’s customers. Menck continues to operate as a standalone business, preserving its independent market position. The transaction was financed through available liquidity and a EUR 380 million acquisition facility. Menck contributed approximately EUR 24.1 million of revenue and EUR 1.1 million of net profit from 11 August to 30 September 2026.

Backlog and commercial momentum

As of 23 November 2026, Cadeler’s contract backlog, including options, stands at EUR 2.4 billion.

The backlog includes a firm contract, signed after the reporting period, to support the transportation and installation of wind turbines at Dogger Bank C in the UK, the third 1.2GW phase of the world’s largest offshore wind farm under construction and the operational debut for Wind Apex.

Cadeler also announced the signing of a significant exclusivity agreement (not included in the group’s contract backlog) with an undisclosed client for wind turbine and foundation installation at a large-scale offshore wind farm in the UK. That installation campaign is expected to commence in 2030, with the foundations campaign to be executed using an A-class vessel and an O-class vessel, and the wind turbines to be installed by a P-class vessel.

Fleet expansion and newbuild programme

By mid-2027, Cadeler expects to operate a 12-vessel fleet, the largest and most versatile in the offshore wind industry.

Wind Ace joined the fleet in July 2026 on schedule and within budget. Designed for both foundation and turbine installation, its first project will be ScottishPower Renewables’ East Anglia TWO, where offshore installation is planned to begin in 2027. The construction of Cadeler’s third A-class vessel, Wind Apex, is similarly progressing on schedule.

In August, Cadeler signed firm contracts with COSCO Shipping Offshore for two T-class vessels, due for delivery in 2030 and 2031. Incorporating breakthrough technologies, the T-class vessels will be the largest and most capable vessels in the offshore installation and foundation market.

Redomiciliation to the United Kingdom

Cadeler successfully completed its redomiciliation to the United Kingdom on 4 November 2026, following acceptance of the voluntary share exchange offer by holders representing 92.06% of Cadeler A/S shares. Cadeler plc’s shares began trading on the Oslo and New York stock exchanges on 5 November 2026. Cadeler plc intends to acquire the remaining 7.94% of Cadeler A/S shares for approximately EUR 173 million. The establishment of a UK-incorporated parent company positions the Group to attract a broader and more diverse international investor base, while creating a corporate structure that better reflects the scale and global reach of Cadeler’s activities. The redomiciliation will have no impact on Cadeler’s personnel, geographic footprint or project operations.

Strong balance sheet and strategic financing initiatives

As of 30 September 2026, Cadeler’s total assets stood at EUR 4.5 billion, up 31+% year-to-date. This includes a EUR 484 million increase in property, plant and equipment, primarily attributable to newbuilds and various vessel upgrades, as well as the acquisition of Menck. Total equity increased to EUR 1.9 billion as of 30 September 2026, reflecting an increase of EUR 347 million from the balance at year end 2025 of EUR 1.5 billion.

In July 2026, Cadeler announced the signing of an EIFO-backed green term loan facility of EUR 247 million to fund the delivery of Wind Apex, expected in Q2 2027.

Earnings Call

In connection with the publication of its Q3 2026 Earnings Release, Cadeler will host a live video webcast presentation for the investment community. Mikkel Gleerup, Chief Executive Officer, and Peter Brogaard Hansen, Chief Financial Officer, will present live from London.

Date: 23 November 2026
Time: 08:00 EST / 13:00 UK / 14:00 CET

The earnings presentation is open to all interested parties and may include forward-looking information. Please register in advance at this link https://cadeler-q3-2026-earnings-presentation.open-exchange.net/registration.

A replay of the webcast and the presentation slides will be made available on Cadeler’s Investor Relations website following the presentation, available here: http://www.cadeler.com/investor.

The company owns and operates the industry’s largest fleet of jack-up offshore wind installation vessels and is expanding its capabilities into full-scope foundation transport and installation, as well as operations & maintenance. With its modern fleet and depth of expertise across onshore and offshore operations, Cadeler supports the safe, efficient and reliable delivery of offshore wind projects worldwide. HALIFAX, NS, Nov. 21, 2026 /PRNewswire/ -- Isar Aerospace ("Isar") and Maritime Launch Services ("MLS") (TSX: MAXQ) (OTCQB: MAXQF) are taking the next step in advancing Canadian space capabilities with the transition of a dedicated launch complex at Spaceport Nova Scotia to Isar. This marks the moment at which Isar assumes operational responsibility for its own launch infrastructure on Canadian soil and the beginning of construction on what will become Isar's dedicated launch pad in Canada.

The handover is a key milestone in the two companies' partnership, under which Isar will develop, build and operate a dedicated launch complex, including a final assembly line and a payload preparation facility, for its Spectrum launch vehicle. First orbital launches are targeted for 2028. The announcement comes with the support of the Canadian government, reflecting shared priorities in sovereign space capability and defence cooperation.

In September this year, Isar successfully reached orbit on its second mission, becoming the first European commercial space company to deliver satellites into orbit. As the company ramps up production of its in-house-developed launch vehicle at its purpose-built factory near Munich – with capacity of 40 vehicles per year – it is also expanding its global launch site network. Spaceport Nova Scotia will be Isar's second launch site globally, and its first in North America.

"Starting construction on our launch complex at Spaceport Nova Scotia brings us a decisive step closer to launching from Canadian soil. But our ambition goes far beyond building a launch site. Together with Maritime Launch Services, we want to advance Canada's space ecosystem and establish sovereign access to orbit as a lasting national capability – one that strengthens Canada's role as a space nation and the Alliance's capabilities for years to come," said Stella Guillen, Chief Commercial Officer of Isar Aerospace.

"Today's handover marks an important step in the development of Spaceport Nova Scotia and demonstrates the strength of our multi-user spaceport model. Isar Aerospace's investment advances sovereign launch capability in Canada, strengthens cooperation between allies, and brings foreign direct investment and jobs to Nova Scotia and the communities surrounding the spaceport. It also strengthens Nova Scotia's position in the global space economy and Canada's role as a spacefaring nation," said Stephen Matier, President and CEO of Maritime Launch Services.

Spaceport Nova Scotia, developed by Maritime Launch Services Inc., is a multi-user orbital launch facility, located near the rural communities of Canso, Hazel Hill and Little Dover. Designed to support multiple launch providers and customers, its location on Nova Scotia's Atlantic coast provides over-ocean launch trajectories and access to mid- to high-inclination and polar orbits. The site will support Earth observation, communications and defence missions for government and commercial operators alike.

Isar's investment aligns directly with Canada's Defence Industrial Strategy and the Canadian Space Launch Act, both of which identify and prioritize sovereign launch capability as a national priority. As a company that designs, manufactures and operates its own launch vehicles, Isar brings integrated end-to-end launch expertise to a facility built to support Canadian and allied missions.

"Canada's sovereignty extends beyond our borders and into space. This partnership between Maritime Launch Services and Germany's Isar Aerospace is an important step toward building a sovereign space-launch capability right here in Canada. It will strengthen our national security, create new opportunities for Canadian industry, and deepen our defence cooperation with Germany. As space becomes increasingly critical to our security and our economy, Canada must have the ability to launch and protect the capabilities we depend on," said the Honourable David J. McGuinty, Minister of National Defence.

"Companies are turning to Nova Scotia to make world-class ideas into solutions, showing Nova Scotia's unique strength in the aerospace and defence sector. Congratulations to Isar and Maritime Launch Services for advancing critical launch infrastructure that will strengthen Canada's position in the global space economy and create high-value opportunities for Nova Scotians well beyond the launch pad", said the Honourable Colton LeBlanc, Minister of Growth, Development and Defence Industries, Province of Nova Scotia.

About Isar Aerospace
The European space company Isar Aerospace offers launch services for transporting small and medium-sized satellites and satellite constellations into Earth orbit. The launch vehicles used to transport these satellites are developed, manufactured, and tested almost entirely in-house. Headquartered near Munich, Germany, Isar Aerospace was founded in 2018 and has grown to over 400 employees, working across 5 international locations. Private funding from international investors provides strong backing for the company's pioneering approach to scale and industrialize launch vehicle production through vertical integration.

Third Quarter of 2026 Financial Results

Revenues

Revenue reached US$68.3 million, representing a year-over-year decrease of 9.9% and a quarter-over-quarter increase of 7.5%. The year-over-year decline was due to the broader macroeconomic environment and a strong comparison base, as well as supply constraints on top-selling offerings, particularly Helio Strap and Balance 3. However, revenue from the Active series increased significantly year-over-year.

Gross Margin

Gross margin was 35.0%, compared with 38.2% and 37.4% in the same period of 2025 and the second quarter of 2026, respectively. Gross margin faced several headwinds during the quarter, primarily elevated memory and other component costs, as well as foreign currency impacts. While product mix improved year-over-year, supported by new product introductions including the Active series, this favorable mix benefit was more than offset by higher memory costs within our entry-level price segments. Gross margin for the second quarter of 2026 benefited from tariff refunds that the Company recorded related to duties previously remitted under the International Emergency Economic Powers Act ("IEEPA"). Excluding the impact of these refunds, gross margin increased sequentially.

Research and Development Expenses

Research and development expenses in the third quarter of 2026 were US$11.4 million, compared with US$10.8 million and US$11.5 million in the third quarter of 2025 and the second quarter of 2026, respectively. Excluding US$0.6 million of foreign currency headwinds, research and development expenses were flat compared with the same period of 2025. We continued to invest in a series of cutting-edge products as well as new technologies, including AI, to maintain our competitive edge against our peers. At the same time, we focused on refined research and development approaches, consistently evaluating resource efficiency to optimize return on investment and productivity.

Selling and Marketing Expenses

Selling and marketing expenses in the third quarter of 2026 were US$18.0 million, compared with US$12.0 million and US$18.3 million in the third quarter of 2025 and the second quarter of 2026, respectively. The US$6.0 million year-over-year increase was primarily attributable to US$1.9 million investment across online and offline channels for content refreshes, in-store displays and holiday season readiness, and US$1.5 million of launch campaigns for new products including the Balance 3, Balance Ultra and T-Rex Dual Solar. The remainder of the increase reflected US$1.4 million for marathons, Ultra-Trail du Mont-Blanc (UTMB) and media sponsorships, and US$1.2 million related to the HYROX and new athletes partnerships.

General and Administrative Expenses

General and administrative expenses were US$5.6 million in the third quarter of 2026, compared with US$7.0 million and US$6.2 million in the third quarter of 2025 and the second quarter of 2026, respectively. We continued to streamline overhead, maintaining disciplined cost control while improving operating efficiency.

Operating Expenses

GAAP and adjusted operating expenses[2] for the third quarter of 2026 were US$35.0 million and US$34.2 million, respectively, compared with US$29.8 million and US$28.6 million in the third quarter of 2025, and US$36.0 million and US$34.8 million in the second quarter of 2026. Out of the year-over-year increase of US$5.2 million in operating expenses, US$0.8 million was due to foreign currency impacts. The remaining US$4.4 million was primarily due to higher selling and marketing expenses as mentioned above. On a quarter-over-quarter basis, operating expenses decreased slightly.

Operating Income/(Loss)

GAAP and adjusted operating results[3] were loss of US$11.1 million and loss of US$10.3 million, respectively, compared with loss of US$0.9 million and income of US$0.4 million in the same quarter of 2025. The net operating loss was due to lower gross margin mainly resulting from higher memory and other component costs and foreign currency headwinds, as well as increased investment in marketing and branding activities, but the operating loss narrowed compared with the second quarter of 2026. 

Net Income/(Loss)

GAAP and adjusted net loss attributable to Zepp for the third quarter of 2026 were US$12.6 million and US$11.6 million, respectively, compared with GAAP and adjusted net loss of US$1.6 million and US$0.7 million for the same quarter in 2025. The US$10.9 million year-over-year increase in adjusted net loss was primarily driven by a US$6.0 million increase in selling and marketing expenses, as discussed above, followed by a US$3.2 million unfavorable foreign exchange impact. In addition, higher memory and other component costs resulted in a net US$2.7 million gross profit headwind, partially mitigated by a more favorable product mix. These unfavorable impacts were partially offset by US$1.1 million in savings from general and administrative expenses.
